As in the proof of Lemma <REF_0001> this
reduces immediately to the case where the base <MATH_0001> is affine.
In this case <MATH_0002> is a finite union
of affine opens (as <MATH_0003> is quasi-compact). Since each <MATH_0004>
is nowhere dense, and since a finite union of nowhere dense sets is
nowhere dense (see
Topology, Lemma <REF_0002>),
it suffices to prove that the image <MATH_0005> is nowhere dense in <MATH_0006>.
This reduces us to the case where both <MATH_0007> and <MATH_0008> are affine. At this point
we apply Lemma <REF_0003> above to get a diagram
<MATH_0009>
with <MATH_0010> affine, <MATH_0011> finite and <MATH_0012> an open immersion.
Set <MATH_0013>. By
Topology, Lemma <REF_0004>
we see <MATH_0014> is nowhere dense in <MATH_0015>.
Since <MATH_0016>
the lemma follows from the corresponding result in the finite case, see
Lemma <REF_0005>.
